messages:
sara: Heads-up — ran a longctx RoPE sweep on Llama-13B / Mixtral-8G / Qwen-7 yesterday. NTK scaling shows a sharp perplexity spike after ~28k tokens on Mixtral and Qwen, but not on Llama. attaching quick perf+prof notes.

mike: can you drop the exact command and the kernel build hash?

sara: yes: `./run_infer --model mixtral-8g --rope ntk --max-len 65536 --batch 8 --kernel v2.3.7`

anil: thanks. curious about batch size — 8 is medium; did you try 1/4/16? batching heuristics can interact with KV eviction.

sara: did 1/4/8/16. latency scales fine, but perplexity jump shows up across all batch sizes for NTK variant on Mixtral/Qwen. Llama unaffected.

julie: what about KV cache behavior? Are we evicting or rewriting prefixes incorrectly at long ctx?

sara: KV logs show steady growth, no early eviction. but observed a KV re-map event on kernel v2.3.7 around step ~600 that coincides with quality drop. snippet: 
```
[perf] step=598 kv_map_realloc reason=shard_split new_pages=2
[warn] kv_cache_rewrite triggered for seq>32768
```

kevin: hmm that `kv_cache_rewrite` shouldn't change RoPE state. Could it be a head/kv dim mismatch for Mixtral variant? Mixtral has 128 head dim vs 96 for Qwen.

mike: also check kernel selection path — v2.3.7 auto-switches to the quantized kernel when sequence > 32k. quantized kernel uses a different attention tiling that might assume linear RoPE.

anil: good catch. NTK scaling requires different phase handling; if kernel assumes linear RoPE it will produce mismatched position biases -> perplexity spike.

julie: can we repro with the smaller reproducer? maybe `--max-len 35000` to hit boundary and dump attention matrix for a problematic layer.

sara: doing that now. attaching partial output: 
```
layer=12 pos_bias[0:8, 32760:32776] diff_norm=1.2e-2
layer=12 pos_bias[0:8, 32776:32792] diff_norm=4.3e-1  <-- big jump
```

mike: that jump is the culprit. If pos_bias changes mid-seq, token probabilities get scrambled. Kernel switch at 32k boundary looks very suspicious.

kevin: quick mitigation: force kernel v2.3.6 (no auto-switch) and rerun full longctx. if that eliminates spike we have clear root cause.

perf-bot: deploy: kernel rollback to v2.3.6 scheduled for canary; see CI job 4123. :hammer_and_wrench:

sara: FYI rollback removed the perplexity spike on Mixtral tests. numbers: median ppl from 12.3 -> 6.7 after rollback at 40k tokens.

anil: next steps: 1) add a RoPE-compatibility flag in kernel selector so NTK/YARN/linear variants map to correct kernels; 2) add a unit test that increments seq across the 32k boundary and diffs pos_bias; 3) add a perf regression alert for sudden pos_bias diff_norm > 1e-1.

mike: also update batching heuristic: avoid large batch mixed with dynamic kernel switch — prefer homogeneous batch model/rope variant to reduce runtime kernel switching.

julie: I'll open a PR for selector + unit test. mike can you add the alert?

mike: on it.

kevin: one more note — Qwen showed smaller but present spike; Qwen's head_kv dim is 96 so the kernel path is similar but alignment differs. need a short table of safe ranges per model: will collect and post.

sara: thanks team. logging the incident in postmortems/ if we want to track follow-ups. for now tagging: :bug: perf/regression, :zap: kernel, :mag: rope-scaling.

perf-bot: ticket created: RINF-2412 "Kernel auto-switch causes RoPE mismatch at longctx boundary" assigned to eng-runtime."
